question: True or false: an application written for IBM's System/360 in the 1960s can still run unchanged on IBM's current mainframes?
answer: True. IBM has made each mainframe architecture a superset of the last, so programs built for the 1964 System/360 still execute on today's Z machines, and banks and insurers run code decades old. Some payroll runs today on instructions first defined when Lyndon Johnson was president.
move: Where rewriting is costly, the old code outlives every machine it ran on.
trap: Judging all computers by phones and laptops that age out within years.
reference: IBM, z/Architecture Principles of Operation, SA22-7832, 2022
